results.name: Lying Leg Raise
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your legs extended and your arms at your sides, palms facing down firm on the floor.
Engage your core muscles and press your lower back into the floor.
Keeping your legs straight, lift them up towards the ceiling until they are perpendicular to the floor.
Slowly lower your legs back to the starting position with control, stopping just before they touch the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you lift your legs up and inhale as you lower them back down.
Keep your legs as straight as possible for maximum effectiveness.
Focus on engaging your abdominal muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Lying Leg Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Hip Flexors, Lower Back.

results.name: Med Ball Half Kneeling Wood Choppers
instructions: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat in front, holding a medicine ball with both hands.
Start with the ball beside your hip on the side of the down knee.
Rotate your torso and lift the ball diagonally across your body to above the opposite shoulder.
Return along the same path with control, then switch sides after the set.
tips: Keep your hips facing forward and squeeze the glute of the down leg.
Move with control; let your torso, not your arms, do the work.
results.description: Med Ball Half Kneeling Wood Choppers is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Shoulders, Glutes.

results.name: Med Ball Toe Touches
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs raised straight toward the ceiling.
Hold a medicine ball with both hands above your chest, arms straight.
Curl your shoulders off the floor and reach the ball up toward your toes.
Lower your shoulders with control and repeat.
tips: Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
Exhale as you reach up.
results.description: Med Ball Toe Touches is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Obliques.

results.name: Medicine Ball Chest Throw With Abs
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent, facing a partner or a wall, holding a medicine ball at your chest.
Curl up into a sit-up and, as you rise, throw the ball forcefully from your chest.
Catch the ball, or receive it back from your partner, at chest height.
Lower your back to the floor with control and repeat.
tips: Brace your core before each throw.
Use a ball you can throw with full speed and good form.
results.description: Medicine Ball Chest Throw With Abs is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Triceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Medicine Ball Rotational Throw
instructions: Stand side-on to a wall about an arm's length away, feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball at your hip.
Load by rotating your torso away from the wall and bending your knees slightly.
Drive from your legs and hips and rotate explosively to throw the ball into the wall.
Catch the rebound, reset and repeat, then switch sides.
tips: Pivot your back foot so the power comes from your hips.
Keep your arms relaxed; they guide the ball, the core throws it.
results.description: Medicine Ball Rotational Throw is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Shoulders, Glutes.

results.name: Middle Crunches
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended straight on the floor and your arms straight by your sides, palms facing the floor.
Curl your abdomen, raising your upper back off the floor, while simultaneously lifting your legs straight up towards the ceiling and raise your arms towards your feet.
Just before your hands and feet touch, lower your upper back, legs and arms back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you lift your upper back, legs and arms up, and inhale as you lower them back down.
Keep your legs as straight as possible for maximum abdominal activation.
Focus on engaging your abdominal muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Middle Crunches is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Lower Back.

results.name: Mountain Climber
instructions: Begin in a plank position on your toes and hands, with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your right knee and bring it towards your right elbow and stop when your knee is close to the elbow.
Return to the starting plank position, then repeat the movement on the opposite side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure you keep your movements smooth and controlled to maintain form and avoid injury.
Maintain a steady breathing pattern, exhaling as you bring your knee towards your elbow and inhaling as you return to the plank position.
Keep your shoulders stable and your core engaged throughout the exercise to enhance effectiveness.
results.description: Mountain Climber is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

results.name: Oblique Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Place your hands behind your head, keeping your elbows wide.
Engage your core muscles and lift your upper back off the floor, rotating your abdomen to raise your right elbow towards the ceiling.
Squeeze your obliques at the top of the movement and slowly lower your upper back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides to work the opposite oblique.
tips: Exhale as you lift and rotate your upper body, and inhale as you lower it back down.
Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands; let your abs do the work.
Focus on engaging your oblique muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Oblique Crunch is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Over Head Weight Sit Up
instructions: Begin by lying flat on your back with your legs slightly bent and your feet together. Hold a weight plate with both hands, extending your arms straight above your chest.
Engage your core muscles and lift your upper body off the floor into a sitting position while keeping the weight extended straight up.
As you sit up, ensure your back remains straight and your chest is lifted, bringing your torso to an upright position.
Lower your upper body back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the entire movement to maintain stability and proper form.
Avoid using momentum to lift your upper body; focus on using your abdominal muscles to perform the sit-up.
Exhale as you sit up and inhale as you lower back down.
results.description: Over Head Weight Sit Up is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Over Weight Ab Crunch
instructions: Begin by lying on your back with your legs straight on the floor close together. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, keeping your arms bent and behind your head, close to the floor.
Engage your core muscles and lift your torso off the floor while bending your knees and raising them to your chest, and bringing the dumbbell close to your knees.
Lower your body back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you crunch up and inhale as you lower back down.
Start with a lighter weight to master the form before progressing to heavier weights.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and avoid injury.
results.description: Over Weight Ab Crunch is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.
